question: Which part of Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part V.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The election of the Vice-President of India is dealt with under Part V (The Union) of the Indian Constitution, specifically Article 66. (भारत के उपराष्ट्रपति का चुनाव — भाग V)

 

• Part V covers Articles 52 to 151 and deals with the Union Executive (President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, Attorney-General), Parliament, and related matters such as the CAG.

 

• The Vice-President is elected by members of an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and voting is by secret ballot.

 

• The office of Vice-President is modelled on the American vice-presidency and was also present in the earlier Constitution of India Bill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vice-President also serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64.

 

• The term of office of the Vice-President is five years, and there is no bar on re-election.

 

NOTE

 

• Part IV (Option 1): Contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36-51), not related to elections.

 

• Part III (Option 2): Contains the Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35).

 

• Part VI (Option 3): Deals with the States, including the State Legislature and the Governor (Articles 152-237).

question: In which of the following games is the ‘Baulk Line’ used?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kabaddi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Kabaddi, the Baulk Line is a line drawn on each half of the court, 3.75 m from the centre line, that a raider must cross to make a valid raid. (बॉक लाइन — कबड्डी)

 

• The Kabaddi court also has a Bonus Line (1 m beyond the Baulk Line) which, if crossed by a raider with one foot while the other is in the air, earns a bonus point provided at least six defenders are on the mat.

 

• A standard Kabaddi court measures 13m x 10m for men and is divided into two equal halves by the centre line.

 

• The term is unique to Kabaddi among the games listed; it is not used in Badminton, Tennis, or Kho-Kho.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabaddi is India's indigenous contact sport and was included in the Asian Games since 1990 (Beijing).

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) is India's premier professional kabaddi tournament, launched in 2014.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 2): Uses terms such as the service line, short service line, and doubles long service line, not a baulk line.

 

• Tennis (Option 3): Uses terms such as the baseline, service line, and centre service line.

 

• Kho-Kho (Option 4): Uses terms such as the central lane and cross lanes.

question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
option_1: Light year is the unit of distance.
option_2: Light year is the distance travelled by light in one year.
option_3: Light year is the unit of time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Light year is the unit of time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A light year is a unit of distance, not time — it is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in one Julian year, so Statement 3 is factually incorrect and hence the answer to this "NOT correct" question. (प्रकाश वर्ष — दूरी की इकाई, समय की नहीं)

 

• One light year is approximately 9.46 × 10^12 km (about 9.46 trillion kilometres).

 

• Light years are used to measure astronomical distances, such as the distance between stars and galaxies, because such distances are too large to conveniently express in kilometres.

 

• Angstrom (Å) is indeed a unit of length, used for extremely small distances such as atomic radii and wavelengths of light; 1 Å = 10^-10 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other astronomical distance units include the Astronomical Unit (AU) — average Earth-Sun distance (~1.496 × 10^8 km) — and the Parsec, which equals about 3.26 light years.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Light year is the unit of distance): This statement is correct, so it is not the answer.

 

• Option 2 (distance travelled by light in one year): This is the correct definition of light year, so this statement is correct.

 

• Option 4 (Angstrom is unit of length): This statement is correct, as explained above.

question: What is the economic justification for subsidies in the agriculture sector?
option_1: It is mostly used to provide benefits for rich farmers.
option_2: It is a part of government expenditure in the service sector.
option_3: It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.
option_4: It is used to provide benefits for capital goods producers in agriculture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is an incentive to provide the benefits of advanced technology and decrease the cost of production.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Agricultural subsidies in India (on fertilizers, seeds, irrigation, power, credit, etc.) are primarily justified on the ground that they act as an incentive for farmers to adopt modern technology and inputs, which lowers the per-unit cost of production and boosts productivity. (कृषि सब्सिडी — उन्नत तकनीक अपनाने हेतु प्रोत्साहन)

 

• By reducing the cost of inputs such as fertilizers and irrigation, subsidies make it financially viable for small and marginal farmers to use high-yielding seed varieties, chemical fertilizers, and modern irrigation methods.

 

• Subsidies also help stabilise farm incomes, encourage food security, and correct market failures such as the underinvestment in new technology that would occur without government support.

 

• They are not primarily intended to benefit only rich farmers or capital goods producers — their core economic rationale is technology diffusion and cost reduction across the farming community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major agricultural subsidies in India include the fertilizer subsidy, the Minimum Support Price (MSP) mechanism, crop insurance (PMFBY), and interest subvention on crop loans.

 

• Economists debate that untargeted subsidies (e.g., on urea) can lead to overuse and environmental damage, prompting a shift towards schemes like Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (benefits for rich farmers): This is a criticism/side-effect sometimes associated with subsidies, not their stated economic justification.

 

• Option 2 (part of government expenditure in service sector): Agriculture is a primary sector activity, not the service sector, so this is incorrect.

 

• Option 4 (benefits for capital goods producers): Subsidies are targeted at farmers/cultivators, not capital goods producers.

question: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 empowers the _________ to establish authorities charged with the mandate of preventing environmental pollution in all its forms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Central Government.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted under Article 253 of the Constitution, following the Bhopal Gas Tragedy (1984), to provide for the protection and improvement of the environment. (पर्यावरण संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1986 — केंद्र सरकार)

 

• Section 3 of the Act empowers the Central Government to take all measures necessary to protect and improve environmental quality, and it may establish authorities/agencies to exercise these powers on its behalf, such as the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

 

• The Act is often called the 'umbrella legislation' for environmental protection in India, as it fills gaps in other existing environmental laws (Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981).

 

• It gives the Central Government wide powers, including setting standards for emission/discharge of pollutants, restricting areas for industries, and laying down procedures for handling hazardous substances.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under this Act, the Central Government notified the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification and various rules such as the Hazardous Waste Management Rules and E-Waste Management Rules.

 

• The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established later, in 2010, under a separate Act, to deal specifically with environmental disputes.

 

NOTE

 

• State Government (Option 1): State Pollution Control Boards implement environmental laws at the state level, but the power to establish authorities under this Act rests with the Central Government.

 

• Supreme Court (Option 3): The Supreme Court adjudicates environmental disputes but does not derive authority-establishing powers from this Act.

 

• Local municipalities (Option 4): Municipalities implement civic environmental measures (e.g., waste management) but are not empowered by this specific provision.

question: Which of the following Articles and Parts of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part VI of the Indian Constitution deals with 'The States', and its Chapter III (Articles 168 to 212) specifically deals with the State Legislature. (राज्य विधानमंडल — अनुच्छेद 168-212, भाग VI)

 

• Article 168 provides for the constitution of State Legislatures (Legislative Assembly, and Legislative Council where it exists); subsequent articles cover composition, duration, sessions, qualifications, powers, privileges, and legislative procedure.

 

• Part VI as a whole spans Articles 152 to 237 and also covers the Governor (Chapter II), the State Executive, the High Courts, and the Subordinate Courts.

 

• Only six states currently have a Legislative Council (bicameral legislature): Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Union Legislature (Parliament) is dealt with separately under Articles 79 to 122 in Part V.

 

• Panchayats are covered under Articles 243 to 243-O in Part IX, added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI): These articles actually deal with the High Courts in the States, not the State Legislature.

 

• Option 3 (Articles 243 to 243-O in Part IX): This range deals with Panchayats (local self-government), not the State Legislature.

 

• Option 4 (Articles 79 to 122 in Part V): This range deals with Parliament (the Union Legislature), not the State Legislature.

question: The upper portion of the Earth is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lithosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lithosphere is the solid, rocky outer/upper layer of the Earth, comprising the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle. (स्थलमंडल — पृथ्वी का ऊपरी ठोस भाग)

 

• It is the layer on which we live, and it includes landmasses (continents) as well as the ocean floor.

 

• The lithosphere is broken into large and small tectonic plates that move over the underlying, more plastic asthenosphere, causing earthquakes, volcanism, and mountain building.

 

• Its average thickness is about 100 km, though it varies between oceanic (thinner) and continental (thicker) regions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Earth's structure/spheres also include the Atmosphere (gaseous envelope), Hydrosphere (water bodies), and Biosphere (zone of life).

 

• Internally, the Earth is divided into the Crust, Mantle, and Core (inner and outer core), based on composition and physical state.

 

NOTE

 

• Stratosphere (Option 1): A layer of the atmosphere, located above the troposphere, containing the ozone layer.

 

• Troposphere (Option 2): The lowermost layer of the atmosphere, where weather phenomena occur, not part of the solid Earth.

 

• Mesosphere (Option 4): A layer of the atmosphere above the stratosphere, known for meteor burn-up.

question:
Match the following social reform organisations with their respective founders.

Social reform organisations

a) Brahmo Samaj

b) Ramakrishna Mission

c) Prarthana Samaj

d) Arya Samaj

Their founders

i. Swami Vivekanand

ii. Atmaram Pandurang

iii. Raja Ram Mohan Roy

iv. Dayananda Saraswati
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Calcutta. (ब्रह्म समाज — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897, in memory of his guru Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

 

• Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 in Bombay, later guided by figures like M.G. Ranade.

 

• Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875, with the motto 'Back to the Vedas'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is often called the 'Father of Indian Renaissance' and was also instrumental in the abolition of Sati (1829).

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was inspired by and closely associated with the Brahmo Samaj and focused on theistic and social reform in Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i): Incorrectly matches Brahmo Samaj with Atmaram Pandurang and Ramakrishna Mission with Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

• Option 3 (a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i): Incorrectly matches Brahmo Samaj with Dayananda Saraswati and Arya Samaj with Swami Vivekanand.

 

• Option 4 (a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii): Incorrectly matches Brahmo Samaj with Swami Vivekanand and Ramakrishna Mission with Atmaram Pandurang.

question: In West Bengal, how many rice crops are grown in a year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In West Bengal, farmers grow three crops of rice in a year, known as Aus, Aman, and Boro. (पश्चिम बंगाल — तीन धान की फसलें: औस, अमन, बोरो)

 

• Aman (winter rice) is the main/principal crop, sown with the onset of the monsoon (June-July) and harvested in November-December; it accounts for the largest share of production.

 

• Aus (autumn rice) is sown in pre-monsoon months (March-April) and harvested in the monsoon (July-August), while Boro (summer rice) is grown in winter using irrigation and harvested in summer (April-May).

 

• This multiple-cropping pattern is possible due to West Bengal's fertile alluvial soil, ample rainfall, and extensive irrigation network in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• West Bengal is one of India's largest rice-producing states, along with Uttar Pradesh and Punjab.

 

• Rice is a kharif crop predominantly, requiring high temperature and rainfall (over 100 cm), and thrives well in the deltaic and coastal regions of eastern and southern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (Two/Four/One): These do not match the well-established three-crop pattern (Aus, Aman, Boro) followed in West Bengal's rice cultivation.

question: Which of the following sectors in India faces seasonal unemployment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are without work for certain months of the year, and it is most prominently seen in the agricultural sector in India. (मौसमी बेरोजगारी — कृषि क्षेत्र)

 

• Farm labour is required intensively during sowing and harvesting seasons, but demand for labour drops sharply in the off-season, leaving many agricultural workers without work for part of the year.

 

• This form of unemployment is a major concern in India because a large proportion of the workforce still depends on agriculture, which itself provides work for only part of the year in most regions lacking irrigation for multiple cropping.

 

• Government schemes like MGNREGA aim to provide alternative employment to rural workers during the agricultural off-season.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other types of unemployment in India include disguised unemployment (also common in agriculture, where more people are engaged than needed), structural unemployment, and cyclical unemployment.

 

• The share of agriculture in India's GDP has been declining, but its share in employment remains disproportionately high, which is one of the structural challenges of the Indian economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Manufacturing (Option 2), Medical (Option 3) and Information Technology (Option 4): These sectors typically offer year-round employment and are not characteristically associated with seasonal unemployment in the way agriculture is.

question: The revolution of 1857 started in May from which of the following cantonments in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meerut.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revolt of 1857 broke out on 10 May 1857 at the Meerut cantonment, when sepoys of the Bengal Army rebelled against the introduction of the new Enfield rifle cartridges, rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat. (1857 का विद्रोह — मेरठ छावनी)

 

• The immediate trigger was the court-martial and imprisonment of 85 sepoys of the 3rd Native Cavalry at Meerut on 9 May 1857 for refusing to use the cartridges.

 

• From Meerut, the rebel sepoys marched to Delhi and proclaimed the aged Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as the symbolic leader (Shahenshah-e-Hindustan) of the uprising.

 

• The revolt subsequently spread to other cantonments including Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, and Bareilly, led respectively by figures like Nana Sahib, Begum Hazrat Mahal, and Rani Lakshmibai.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key leaders of the revolt included Nana Sahib (Kanpur), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow), Kunwar Singh (Bihar), and Tantia Tope.

 

• The revolt is variously described as the 'First War of Indian Independence' (V.D. Savarkar) or a 'Sepoy Mutiny' by earlier British historians.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanpur (Option 1): Was a major centre of the revolt under Nana Sahib, but the uprising did not originate here.

 

• Jhansi (Option 2): Rani Lakshmibai led the resistance here, but it was not the starting point of the revolt.

 

• Lucknow (Option 3): Was besieged during the revolt under Begum Hazrat Mahal, but again was not where it began.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of both mammals and birds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Warm blooded.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both mammals and birds are warm-blooded (endothermic) animals, meaning they can internally regulate and maintain a relatively constant body temperature, regardless of the external environment. (गर्म रक्त वाले प्राणी — स्तनधारी और पक्षी)

 

• This endothermy allows mammals and birds to remain active and metabolically efficient across a wide range of climates, unlike cold-blooded (ectothermic) reptiles, amphibians, and fish.

 

• Viviparity (giving birth to live young) is characteristic of most mammals but not birds, which are oviparous (egg-laying).

 

• Pneumatic (air-filled) bones are a special adaptation found in birds to reduce body weight for flight, and are not a mammalian feature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Warm-bloodedness in mammals and birds is supported by features like fur/hair (mammals) and feathers (birds), which provide insulation, along with a four-chambered heart in both groups for efficient circulation.

 

• Mammals are further characterised by mammary glands (for producing milk) and the presence of a diaphragm.

 

NOTE

 

• Viviparity (Option 1): Common in mammals (with exceptions like the egg-laying monotremes) but absent in birds, which always lay eggs.

 

• Pigmented skin (Option 2): Not a defining shared feature distinguishing/uniting mammals and birds specifically.

 

• Pneumatic bones (Option 3): Found only in birds (an adaptation for flight), not in mammals.

question: To promote agriculture, Muhammad Tughlaq founded which of the following new ministries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diwan-i Amir-i kohi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq established the Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi, a separate department/ministry of agriculture, to promote and improve agricultural production. (दीवान-ए-अमीर-ए-कोही — कृषि विभाग, मुहम्मद बिन तुगलक)

 

• This department was tasked with extending cultivation, especially through agricultural loans (sondhar) to peasants for buying seeds, cattle, and implements, and encouraging farmers to switch to more profitable crops.

 

• The scheme was implemented notably in the Doab region, but ultimately failed due to poor administration, corruption among officials, and unfavourable natural conditions like famine.

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq is otherwise well known for controversial measures such as the transfer of capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token/symbolic currency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq (r. 1325-1351) was the son of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, founder of the Tughlaq dynasty, and is remembered by historians as a ruler of bold but often impractical experiments.

 

• He is sometimes called an 'ill-starred idealist' by historian Ziauddin Barani for his ambitious but poorly executed policies.

 

NOTE

 

• Diwan-i-Arz (Option 1): The military department, responsible for the recruitment, organisation and payment of the army; associated with Balban and later formalised under Alauddin Khalji.

 

• Diwan-i-Insha (Option 3): The department of royal correspondence/official communication.

 

• Diwan-i-Risalat (Option 4): The department dealing with religious and charitable matters/appeals (also called Diwan-i-Rasalat).

question: In the context of cell division, which chromosomal behaviour takes place at the leptotene stage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chromosomes begin to condense.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leptotene is the first stage of prophase I of meiosis, during which the chromosomes, already replicated, begin to condense and become visible under the light microscope as long, thin, single threads. (लेप्टोटीन अवस्था — गुणसूत्रों का संघनन प्रारंभ)

 

• During leptotene, the chromosomes are not yet paired; each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids, though these appear as a single thread due to the tightness of association.

 

• The subsequent stages proceed in order: Zygotene (pairing/synapsis of homologous chromosomes begins), Pachytene (synapsis is complete and crossing over occurs), Diplotene (homologous chromosomes start separating, chiasmata become visible), and Diakinesis (terminalisation of chiasmata, chromosomes fully condensed).

 

• Compaction of chromosomes that begins at leptotene continues progressively throughout prophase I.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Meiosis consists of two successive divisions (Meiosis I and II) and produces four haploid daughter cells from one diploid parent cell, essential for sexual reproduction and genetic variation.

 

• Crossing over, which results in genetic recombination, occurs during the pachytene stage between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• Chromosomes are un-synapsed (Option 1): While technically true at leptotene (pairing hasn't started), this describes an absence of a process rather than the defining positive chromosomal behaviour occurring at this stage, which is condensation.

 

• Synapsis is complete (Option 2): This describes the pachytene stage, not leptotene.

 

• Homologous chromosomes pair (Option 3): Pairing (synapsis) begins at the zygotene stage, not leptotene.

question: Arvind Parikh, a Padma Bhushan awardee, plays which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arvind Parikh is a renowned Indian classical musician who plays the Sitar, and is a disciple of the legendary sitar maestro Ustad Vilayat Khan of the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana. (अरविंद पारीख — सितार वादक)

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, in recognition of his contribution to Indian classical music.

 

• Beyond performance, Arvind Parikh has been a noted musicologist, teacher, and patron of Hindustani classical music, and has served in leadership roles with organisations promoting Indian music.

 

• He is also known for balancing a career in business with a lifelong, serious pursuit of classical sitar performance and pedagogy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous sitar players of India include Pandit Ravi Shankar and Ustad Vilayat Khan himself.

 

• The Padma awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri) are India's highest civilian honours, announced annually on Republic Day.

 

NOTE

 

• Bansuri (Option 2): A famous exponent is Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, not Arvind Parikh.

 

• Tabla (Option 3): Famous tabla players include Ustad Zakir Hussain, not Arvind Parikh.

 

• Sarangi (Option 4): Famous sarangi players include Ustad Sultan Khan, not Arvind Parikh.

question: Which playback singer was honoured with the Nightingale of Asia Award in 1987?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Asha Bhosle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Asha Bhosle, the legendary Indian playback singer, was honoured with the title 'Nightingale of Asia' in 1987 in recognition of her extraordinary versatility and vast body of work in playback singing. (एशिया की कोकिला — आशा भोसले)

 

• She is renowned for her vast repertoire spanning classical, pop, ghazals, and film songs across multiple Indian languages, and holds a Guinness World Record for the most studio recordings by any singer.

 

• Asha Bhosle has been honoured with India's civilian awards, the Padma Vibhushan (2008), and prestigious music honours including the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2000) and multiple National Film Awards.

 

• She is the younger sister of the equally legendary playback singer Lata Mangeshkar, who was popularly called the 'Nightingale of India'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asha Bhosle's popular songs span decades of Bollywood music, working extensively with music directors such as O.P. Nayyar and R.D. Burman (whom she later married).

 

• Other legendary Indian female playback singers include Lata Mangeshkar, Geeta Dutt, and Kavita Krishnamurthy.

 

NOTE

 

• Pulapaka Susheela (Option 1): A veteran South Indian playback singer, famous for Telugu, Tamil, and Kannada films, but not the recipient of this particular title.

 

• Mubarak Begum (Option 3): A noted Hindi playback singer known for songs like 'Kabhi Tanhaiyon Mein', but not the title holder here.

 

• Kavita Krishnamurthy (Option 4): A well-known contemporary playback singer, but she was not honoured with this 1987 title.

question:
How many carbon dioxide and water molecules will be there in the product side, if the following equation is made balanced?

C2H5OH+O2→CO2+H2O
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 and 3, respectively.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The combustion of ethanol is represented by the balanced chemical equation: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. (एथेनॉल का दहन — संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण)

 

• Balancing requires equal numbers of each atom on both sides: ethanol (C₂H₅OH) has 2 carbon, 6 hydrogen, and 1 oxygen atoms, so 2 molecules of CO₂ are needed to balance carbon, and 3 molecules of H₂O are needed to balance the 6 hydrogen atoms (3 × 2 = 6).

 

• Balancing oxygen: the product side has (2 × 2) + (3 × 1) = 7 oxygen atoms; since ethanol already supplies 1 oxygen atom, 3 molecules of O₂ (supplying 6 oxygen atoms) are required on the reactant side to make the total 7.

 

• The fully balanced equation is therefore: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, giving 2 CO₂ and 3 H₂O molecules on the product side.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This is an example of a combustion (oxidation) reaction, where a hydrocarbon/alcohol reacts with oxygen to release energy along with carbon dioxide and water.

 

• Balancing chemical equations follows the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass (and hence the number of atoms of each element) is conserved in a chemical reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (3 and 6):, Option 2 (1 and 1):, and Option 4 (3 and 2): These do not satisfy the atom-balance requirements for carbon and hydrogen as shown above, and hence are incorrect.

question: ‘Kuki dance’ is a folk dance of India that is predominantly performed in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Kuki dance' is a folk dance predominantly performed by the Kuki tribal community, and is prominently associated with the state of Nagaland. (कुकी नृत्य — नागालैंड)

 

• It is typically performed during festivals and community celebrations, showcasing vibrant tribal costumes, rhythmic movements and traditional music of the Kuki people.

 

• Nagaland is home to numerous tribal folk dances, reflecting its rich cultural diversity across its various Naga tribes and communities settled there.

 

• The Kuki people are also found in neighbouring states such as Manipur, Mizoram, and Assam, but this dance form is listed among Nagaland's folk dances in the standard exam reference material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known folk dances of Nagaland include the Rengma dance, Zeliang dance, and War dance (Naga tribes' traditional martial performances).

 

• The Hornbill Festival, held every December at Kisama, Nagaland, showcases many such tribal folk dances together.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Yakshagana and Dollu Kunitha, not Kuki dance.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Raslila and Kajri, not Kuki dance.

 

• Rajasthan (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Ghoomar and Kalbelia, not Kuki dance.

question: The term ‘Microfinancing’ was first used in the 1970s during the development of Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, which was founded by ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The term 'Microfinancing' gained prominence in the 1970s with the development of the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh, founded by economist Muhammad Yunus. (मुहम्मद यूनुस — ग्रामीण बैंक, बांग्लादेश)

 

• Muhammad Yunus pioneered the concept of microcredit — providing small, collateral-free loans to poor individuals, particularly women, to help them start income-generating activities and escape poverty.

 

• For this pioneering work, Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

 

• The Grameen Bank model has since been replicated worldwide as an effective tool for financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• In India, microfinance is largely delivered through the Self-Help Group (SHG)-Bank Linkage Programme, pioneered by NABARD, and through Microfinance Institutions (MFIs).

 

• Muhammad Yunus later also served in Bangladesh's interim government, reflecting his continued prominence in public life.

 

NOTE

 

• Adam Smith (Option 2): An 18th-century Scottish economist, known as the 'Father of Economics', unrelated to the Grameen Bank.

 

• Jeremy Bentham (Option 3): A philosopher known for Utilitarianism, unrelated to microfinance.

 

• Alfred Marshall (Option 4): A neoclassical economist known for concepts like elasticity of demand, unrelated to the Grameen Bank.

question: Nirupama Sanjeev is a famous ______ player of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is tennis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nirupama Sanjeev (née Nirupama Vaidyanathan) is a former Indian tennis player, notable for being the first Indian woman to play in the main draw of a Grand Slam tournament (Australian Open, 1998). (निरुपमा संजीव — भारतीय टेनिस खिलाड़ी)

 

• She had a successful career representing India in the Fed Cup (now Billie Jean King Cup) and won multiple national titles.

 

• After retiring from active play, she has contributed to Indian tennis as a coach and administrator, promoting the sport among young players.

 

• Her achievements paved the way for later generations of Indian women's tennis players competing at the international level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Indian women tennis players include Sania Mirza, who achieved further milestones such as reaching World No. 1 in doubles.

 

• India's participation in international tennis includes the Davis Cup (men's) and Billie Jean King Cup (women's) team events.

 

NOTE

 

• Badminton (Option 1): Famous Indian badminton players include PV Sindhu and Saina Nehwal, not Nirupama Sanjeev.

 

• Swimming (Option 2): Nirupama Sanjeev is not associated with swimming.

 

• Chess (Option 4): Famous Indian chess players include Viswanathan Anand, not Nirupama Sanjeev.

question: Who among the following Pallava kings occupied Vatapi (Badami) and defeated the Chalukyas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narasimhavarman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Narasimhavarman I (also known as Mahamalla or Mamalla), a Pallava king, occupied Vatapi (Badami), the capital of the Chalukyas, and decisively defeated the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II around 642 CE. (नरसिंहवर्मन प्रथम — वातापी विजय, पल्लव वंश)

 

• After this victory, Narasimhavarman I assumed the title 'Vatapikonda', meaning 'the conqueror of Vatapi'.

 

• He is also celebrated for constructing the famous rock-cut monuments at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), including the rathas (monolithic temples), which are named after him.

 

• The Pallava-Chalukya rivalry was a long-running conflict for supremacy over the Deccan region, with both dynasties alternately gaining the upper hand over generations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Pallava dynasty ruled over parts of South India (Tamil Nadu) with their capital at Kanchipuram, and were notable patrons of Dravidian architecture.

 

• Pulakeshin II, the Chalukya king defeated by Narasimhavarman I, was himself known for having earlier defeated Harshavardhana of Kannauj.

 

NOTE

 

• Sivaskanda Varman (Option 1): An early Pallava ruler (3rd-4th century CE), known for the Prakrit Mayidavolu and Hirahadagalli copper plate inscriptions, predating this conflict.

 

• Parameswaravarman (Option 2): A later Pallava king who fought further wars with the Chalukyas, but it was Narasimhavarman I who captured Vatapi.

 

• Simhavarman (Option 3): The name of several early Pallava kings, none of whom is credited with the conquest of Vatapi.

question: Who among the following famous badminton players won Singapore Open 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PV Sindhu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian badminton star PV Sindhu won the women's singles title at the Singapore Open 2022, defeating Wang Zhi Yi of China in the final. (पीवी सिंधु — सिंगापुर ओपन 2022 विजेता)

 

• This victory made her the first Indian to win the Singapore Open title and came shortly before her gold medal win at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

• PV Sindhu is a two-time Olympic medallist (Silver at Rio 2016, Bronze at Tokyo 2020) and a former World Champion (2019 BWF World Championships).

 

• She remains one of India's most decorated badminton players, with numerous Super Series/World Tour titles to her name.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• PV Sindhu hails from Hyderabad, Telangana, and has been honoured with India's civilian awards including the Padma Bhushan and Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

 

• Other prominent Indian badminton players include Saina Nehwal (first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal in badminton, Bronze at London 2012) and men's players like Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth.

• Aparna Popat (Option 1): A former Indian badminton champion and multiple-time national champion, but not a Singapore Open 2022 winner.

 

• Saina Nehwal (Option 2): A decorated Indian badminton player and former World No. 1, but she did not win the Singapore Open 2022.

 

• Jwala Gutta (Option 3): A noted Indian doubles specialist, but not associated with the Singapore Open 2022 singles title.

question: The ‘Lokranjan’ festival celebrates the folk and tribal culture of which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 'Lokranjan' festival is an annual cultural festival celebrating the rich folk and tribal culture of Madhya Pradesh, held at Khajuraho. (लोकरंजन महोत्सव — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The festival showcases traditional folk dances, music, and art forms of various tribal and rural communities of the state, promoting cultural heritage and tourism.

 

• It is generally organised alongside or around the well-known Khajuraho Dance Festival, drawing visitors interested in India's classical and folk performing arts.

 

• Madhya Pradesh, often called the 'Heart of India', has a rich tribal population (including Gond, Bhil, and Baiga communities) whose culture the festival aims to celebrate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Madhya Pradesh festivals include the Khajuraho Dance Festival (classical dance) and Tansen Sangeet Samaroh (classical music, held at Gwalior).

 

• Madhya Pradesh is also home to major tribal art forms such as Gond painting, recognised nationally and internationally.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for tribal festivals like Sarhul and Karma, not the Lokranjan festival.

 

• Manipur (Option 3): Known for its own distinct cultural festivals such as Sangai Festival, not Lokranjan.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 4): Known for tribal festivals such as Wangala (Garo) and Shad Suk Mynsiem (Khasi), not Lokranjan.

question: Which of the following are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part IV of the Indian Constitution, spanning Articles 36 to 51, enumerates the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — भाग IV)

 

• The DPSPs are guidelines/instructions for the State to keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws, aimed at establishing a just, welfare-oriented society, though they are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

 

• They were inspired by the Irish Constitution and cover principles such as securing adequate livelihood, equal pay for equal work, promotion of village panchayats, protection of the environment, and separation of judiciary from the executive.

 

• Article 37 explicitly states that DPSPs, while not enforceable in any court, are 'fundamental in the governance of the country' and it is the duty of the State to apply them in making laws.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The DPSPs are broadly classified into socialistic, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual principles based on their underlying philosophy.

 

• Landmark amendments and judicial interpretations (e.g., the 42nd Amendment, 1976, and the Minerva Mills case, 1980) have shaped the balance between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs.

 

NOTE

 

• Fundamental Rights (Option 1): Enumerated in Part III, Articles 12 to 35, not Part IV.

 

• Fundamental Duties (Option 2): Enumerated in Part IVA, Article 51-A, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976.

 

• The Union (Option 4): Refers to Part V of the Constitution (Articles 52-151), not Part IV.

question: The Gandak river is a tributary of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ganga river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Gandak river (also called Narayani/Gandaki in Nepal) is a major left-bank tributary of the Ganga river. (गंडक नदी — गंगा की सहायक नदी)

 

• It originates in the Nepal Himalayas near the Tibet border (formed by the union of the Kali Gandaki and Trishuli rivers), and flows through Nepal and Bihar before joining the Ganga near Patna (Hajipur/Sonepur area), Bihar.

 

• The Gandak is known for its frequent course changes and flooding in the plains of Bihar, making flood management (via the Gandak Barrage/Gandak Project) an important issue in the region.

 

• Along with other Himalayan tributaries like the Ghaghara, Kosi, and Son, the Gandak significantly augments the flow of the Ganga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important left-bank tributaries of the Ganga include the Ghaghara, Gomti, Kosi, while important right-bank tributaries include the Yamuna and Son.

 

• The Gandak Barrage near Valmiki Nagar (Bihar) is a key structure for irrigation and flood control in the Gandak basin, part of the Indo-Nepal Gandak Project.

 

NOTE

 

• Yamuna river (Option 1): The Yamuna is itself a major tributary of the Ganga (right bank), not a river that the Gandak feeds into.

 

• Kaveri river (Option 3): An independent, major river of peninsular/South India, unrelated to the Ganga system.

 

• Brahmaputra river (Option 4): A separate major Himalayan river system flowing through Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Bangladesh, distinct from the Ganga basin.
